title: Shortfalls on Deduction Schedules: Reporting, Liability and Contest (Paystride Earned Wage Access Program Agreement)
content:
When a deduction schedule's due date passes with part of it not remitted, the unremitted part is a shortfall under the Paystride Earned Wage Access Program Agreement; its amount is the schedule's open amount (the schedule amount less the remittances and write-offs pointing to it, plus the remittance returns pointing to it).

## Reporting and booking

The employer reports, for each worker not fully deducted, the reason within the tier's shortfall report period, in business days after the pay date, and one shortfall notice is booked per schedule and reason, with the amount and worker count for that reason. A shortfall notice states the shortfall and moves nothing on what the employer owes.

## Who bears it

The liability map fixes who bears each reason:

- A shortfall because net pay could not cover the deduction, or because employment ended, is provider-absorbed and is written off at once by a write-off pointing to the notice, the worker's own Access plan following its own recovery rules.
- A shortfall from a payroll processing error, a deduction not taken, or an amount deducted but not remitted is employer-liable, stays in what the employer owes, and is due the tier's employer-liable cure period, in business days, after the notice, recorded as the notice's due date.
- An amount the employer gives no reason for in time is booked with reason unreported and is employer-liable.

## Contest

A contested employer-liable shortfall is reclassified only when the contest arrives within the tier's contest window, in business days, after its shortfall notice was booked. Business days are Monday through Friday excluding Federal Reserve holidays, counted from the day after the notice's entry date, and a contest arriving on the last business day is in time. A contest supported by the payroll register showing net pay could not cover the deduction or that employment ended reclassifies that part as provider-absorbed, booked as a write-off pointing to the notice. A shortfall notice is written off at most once. A write-off never exceeds its notice's amount.

The clock starts from the booking date recorded on the shortfall notice, not from a date the employer states.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, five-business-day window, no holidays)

| Notice booked | Last business day of the window | Contest on that day | Contest on the next business day |
|---|---|---|---|
| a Monday | the following Monday | in time | not in time |
| a Friday | the following Friday | in time | not in time |
